newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India languishes, ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India languishes, ends little changed.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) ended little changed ahead of a holiday in Bombay on Wednesday.
"There was relatively little buying, but there was not much selling. There was some two-way business but it was all carried out within the quote so it did not disturb the market.
The James Capel Indian GDR Index rose 0.01 to 65.04 points, a premium of 8.26 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 12.68 points to 3,226.80.
The global depositary receipt for State Bank of India will be priced on Thursday and start trading on Friday.
"We are hearing that it has gone down quite well and the market for the local stock has firmed up," he said.
Among individual stocks, Reliance continued its firmer trend, adding 48 cents to $10.25/$11.25.
"It was probably just a few buyers in a thin market, but the GDR is now at a premium to the underlying for the first time in months ahead of earnings, which are expected to be poor," a trader said.
Elsewhere, East India Hotels fell 75 cents to $18.25/$19.25 and ITC followed the local higher on expectations Britain's BAT will lift its stake, adding 18 cents to $8.75/$9.65.
The Capel Taiwan Index rose 0.01 points 89.94 points a premium of 2.24 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 9.05 to 6,513.73.
The Capel Korea Index fell 0.61 points, 0.87 percent to 69.72 points, a premium of 28.54 percent over the local market.
The Korea Composite Index fell 0.20 points to 789.47 on the first day that the new limit of 20 percent on foreign ownership came into effect.
